scars.title: localhost delegation hung after repo migration
scars.symptom: First task of the census playbook — a directory creation on the control node — hung silently and the play never progressed. Started right after playbooks moved from /etc/ansible into a Gitea-managed directory.
scars.root_cause: The migrated inventory defined localhost explicitly without ansible_connection=local (and inherited SSH-ish vars), so delegate_to: localhost opened an SSH connection to the control node itself, which sat at an invisible auth prompt. When localhost appears nowhere in inventory, Ansible synthesizes an 'implicit localhost' with connection=local; defining it in inventory without that var silently converts local tasks into SSH sessions.
scars.fix: Either remove localhost from inventory (restore the implicit one) or pin it: localhost ansible_connection=local. Verify with ansible-inventory --host localhost and a -vvv run showing 'ESTABLISH LOCAL CONNECTION'.
scars.lesson: delegate_to: localhost means 'use the host NAMED localhost, with ITS variables' — not 'run locally'. And any migration that changes where you run from changes which config and inventory win. ansible-inventory --host is the truth serum.

scars.title: Pipelining band-aid masked a temp-directory disease
scars.symptom: After the same migration, modules failed until [ssh_connection] pipelining = True was set; ad-hoc work leaned on the raw module. Ping then worked, so it 'seemed fixed'.
scars.root_cause: Module execution stages an AnsiballZ payload into the remote temp directory (remote_tmp, default ~/.ansible/tmp) and runs it there. That staging was failing on the targets (temp-dir permissions/home issues). Pipelining bypasses staging by piping module code into the remote Python's stdin — and raw doesn't use Python at all. Both workarounds route AROUND the broken staging path; neither repairs it.
scars.fix: Diagnose the staging failure directly on a target as the automation user: mkdir -p ~/.ansible/tmp, df -h, mount | grep noexec, and check for sudoers requiretty (which also conflicts with pipelining). Fix the target-side condition. Keep pipelining afterward as a legitimate speed setting — not as the cure.
scars.lesson: When a setting change makes an error vanish, ask WHAT the setting bypasses. 'raw works but ping fails' is the classic tell that transport is fine and Python-side module execution is broken. Verify the cure, not the silence.
